name: com.example.backend.admin.AdminAuthIntegrationTest
comment: Acceptance tests for SLICE-002: Admin JWT authentication infrastructure.  Integration tests — loads full Spring context (Security filter chain, JPA, H2). Seeds its own test data in @BeforeEach; cleans up in @AfterEach. No dependency on external systems or pre-existing DB state.  Test method naming: ac003_xxx mirrors ac001_xxx convention from SLICE-001.

methods.name: ac003_validCredentialsReturnJwt
methods.comment: AC-003: Valid admin credentials return 200 with a JWT containing sub + exp + iat.  Given: DB has AdminCredential for testUsername with bcrypt("secret") When:  POST /auth/login {"username": testUsername, "password": "secret"} Then:  200 OK, body.token is a valid JWT with sub == testUsername and exp in the future

methods.name: ac004_invalidCredentialsReturn401
methods.comment: AC-004: Invalid password returns 401 and no token.  Given: DB has AdminCredential for testUsername When:  POST /auth/login with wrong password Then:  401 Unauthorized, body does not contain "token"

methods.name: ac005_missingTokenReturns401
methods.comment: AC-005: Request without JWT is blocked by filter chain with 401 (not 403, not 404).  Given: /admin/protected-test is not declared PUBLIC by any PublicPathContributor When:  GET /admin/protected-test with no Authorization header Then:  401 Unauthorized — filter chain intercepts before routing, so path existence is irrelevant

methods.name: ac006_validJwtIsPassedThroughFilterChain
methods.comment: AC-006: Request with a valid JWT is passed through by filter chain (reaches routing layer).  Given: a legitimately issued JWT (sub=testUsername, exp in future) When:  GET /admin/protected-test with Authorization: Bearer <valid-token> Then:  404 Not Found (routing layer — path does not exist) NOT 401 (which would indicate Security intercepted it)  401 vs 404 is the observable signal for "did the filter chain pass this through?". The non-existent path is intentional: no dependency on SLICE-003 endpoints.

name: com.example.backend.admin.AdminReviewIntegrationTest
comment: Acceptance tests for SLICE-003: Admin application review.  Integration tests — loads full Spring context (Security filter chain, JPA, H2). Seeds its own data in @BeforeEach. Each test is self-contained.

methods.name: ac007_adminCanListPendingApplications
methods.comment: AC-007: Authenticated admin can list PENDING applications; APPROVED ones are excluded.  Given:  2 PENDING applications + 1 APPROVED application in DB When:   GET /admin/applications with valid JWT Then:   200 OK; body is array of 2 entries; each has id, email, name, status=PENDING

methods.name: ac008_adminApprovesApplication
methods.comment: AC-008: Admin approves a PENDING application → status becomes APPROVED, reviewedBy recorded.  Given:  1 PENDING application in DB When:   PATCH /admin/applications/{id}/review {"decision":"APPROVE"} with valid JWT Then:   200 OK; DB record has status=APPROVED, reviewedBy=adminUsername

methods.name: ac009_adminRejectsApplication
methods.comment: AC-009: Admin rejects a PENDING application with a reason → status becomes REJECTED.  Given:  1 PENDING application in DB When:   PATCH /admin/applications/{id}/review {"decision":"REJECT","reason":"資料不完整"} with JWT Then:   200 OK; DB record has status=REJECTED, reviewedBy=adminUsername, rejectionReason not blank

methods.name: ac010_unauthenticatedReviewIsRejected
methods.comment: AC-010: Request without JWT is rejected by the filter chain with 401.  Given:  1 PENDING application in DB When:   PATCH /admin/applications/{id}/review with NO Authorization header Then:   401 Unauthorized; application status unchanged

methods.name: ac011_ac012_approveCreatesAccountAndApproves
methods.comment: AC-011 / AC-012: Admin approves a PENDING application → application APPROVED + Account created.  Given:  1 PENDING application in DB When:   PATCH /admin/applications/{id}/review {"decision":"APPROVE"} with valid JWT Then:   200 OK; response body {applicationStatus:APPROVED, accountCreated:true}; DB: application status=APPROVED; Account with same email exists

methods.name: ac013_partialFailureObservable_stage2FailsDoesNotRevertStage1
methods.comment: AC-013: Stage 2 failure (duplicate email) is observable in response without reverting Stage 1.  Given:  1 PENDING application + an Account with the SAME email already in DB When:   PATCH /admin/applications/{id}/review {"decision":"APPROVE"} with valid JWT Then:   200 OK; response body {applicationStatus:APPROVED, accountCreated:false}; DB: application status=APPROVED (Stage 1 committed); no new Account created

name: com.example.backend.architecture.ArchitectureTest
comment: Phase 3 Layer 2: Architecture rules derived from ARCHITECTURE-LAYERS.md.  Package conventions (per module, e.g. registration): Presentation  : com.example.backend.*.web Application   : com.example.backend.*.application Domain        : com.example.backend.*.domain Infrastructure: com.example.backend.*.infrastructure

methods.name: presentationMustNotDependOnInfrastructure
methods.comment: ARCH-RULE-001: Presentation -> Infrastructure FORBIDDEN

methods.name: applicationMustNotDependOnInfrastructureImpl
methods.comment: ARCH-RULE-002: Application -> Infrastructure impl FORBIDDEN

methods.name: domainMustNotDependOnOtherLayers
methods.comment: ARCH-RULE-003: Domain -> anything FORBIDDEN

methods.name: noLayerShouldDependOnPresentation
methods.comment: ARCH-RULE-004: anything -> Presentation FORBIDDEN

methods.name: applicationTestsMustNotDependOnInfrastructure
methods.comment: ARCH-RULE-005: Test classes in ..application.. must not depend on ..infrastructure..  DO_NOT_INCLUDE_TESTS means ARCH-RULE-002 does not cover test code. This rule closes the gap: unit tests in the Application layer must mock Port interfaces, not wire in Infrastructure implementations directly.

methods.name: onlySecurityModuleCanDependOnSecurityFilterChain
methods.comment: ARCH-RULE-006: SecurityFilterChain must only be referenced inside the security module.  Prevents other modules from declaring their own SecurityFilterChain beans, which would create conflicting filter chain configurations. (See DEC-015: PUBLIC path declaration mechanism)

methods.name: adminMustNotDependOnRegistrationDomainOrInfrastructure
methods.comment: ARCH-RULE-007: admin module must not depend on registration domain or infrastructure.  Enforces DEC-019 (admin = thin Portal): admin may only reference registration's public application-layer UseCase interfaces, never its entities or JPA repositories. Two sub-rules, both must pass.

methods.name: accountApplicationMustNotDependOnInfrastructure
methods.comment: ARCH-RULE-008: account module Application layer must not depend on Infrastructure. Mirrors ARCH-RULE-002 scoped to account module.

methods.name: accountDomainMustNotDependOnOtherLayers
methods.comment: ARCH-RULE-009: account module Domain layer must not depend on other layers. Mirrors ARCH-RULE-003 scoped to account module.

methods.name: adminMustNotDependOnAccountDomainOrInfrastructure
methods.comment: ARCH-RULE-010: admin module must not depend on account domain or infrastructure. Enforces DEC-021: admin accesses account only via CreateAccountUseCase interface.

name: com.example.backend.registration.RegistrationFlowIntegrationTest
comment: Acceptance tests for SLICE-001: Registration flow. Answers: "Can a visitor successfully complete a registration application?"  Integration tests — loads full Spring context (incl. Security filter chain) + H2 in-memory DB. Each test validates one complete vertical path end-to-end, not a unit in isolation.  Test method naming: ac001_xxx mirrors inv001_xxx convention.

methods.name: ac001_newSubmissionCreatesPendingApplication
methods.comment: AC-001: A visitor submitting a valid application receives 201 and the application is persisted as PENDING in the DB.  Given: no PENDING application or APPROVED account exists for the email When:  POST /registrations {"email": "...", "name": "Joe Wang"} Then:  HTTP 201 Created And:   DB registration_applications table has a PENDING record for the email  Also implicitly validates that POST /registrations is not blocked by Spring Security (RegistrationPublicPathContributor is functioning correctly in context).

methods.name: ac002_blankEmailReturnsProblemDetail
methods.comment: AC-002: A visitor submitting a blank email receives 400 Bad Request with ProblemDetail.  Given: system is running When:  POST /registrations {"email": "", "name": "Joe Wang"} Then:  HTTP 400 Bad Request And:   response body is RFC 7807 ProblemDetail  Currently disabled — requires a @ControllerAdvice (or Spring MVC error config) to convert IllegalArgumentException from RegistrationApplicationService → 400. Without it, Spring returns 500 for unhandled exceptions.
